editorial:
You're thrown into a dark future where mutants are hunted by giant robots called Sentinels, and the only hope is sending Wolverine's mind back to the 1970s to stop a war before it starts. The movie brings together the original X-Men cast and their younger versions from First Class, giving you a huge ensemble that actually works. Hugh Jackman anchors everything as Wolverine, while James McAvoy and Michael Fassbender bring real emotion to young Professor X and Magneto. The time travel setup is easy to follow and keeps the stakes high the whole way through.

The action scenes are fantastic, especially the Quicksilver kitchen sequence that will make you grin. The pacing rarely slows down, and the emotional beats land without feeling forced. Some side characters get pushed aside, and the ending wraps things up a little too neatly, but the ride is so fun you won't mind. If you love superhero movies with heart, this is a great pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: Wolverine wakes up in the future and finds that his mission worked. The dark timeline is gone, and the school is alive and well. He sees Jean Grey and Cyclops, who died in earlier films, standing in the hallway, meaning the past was changed enough to save them. Professor X welcomes him back, and everything feels hopeful. The final twist is that Mystique, disguised as William Stryker, pulls Wolverine out of the water instead of the real Stryker, setting up a different future for him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves superhero team-ups and time travel stories.
